hero.headline: Jobless Claims Reach Highest Level Since February
hero.body:
Applications for unemployment benefits climbed to their highest point since February, according to data released by the Labor Department. The increase signals a potential shift in the labor market after months of relative stability.

Weekly jobless claims rose to 225,000, marking a four-month high. The figure represents the number of Americans filing for unemployment assistance for the first time and serves as a proxy for layoffs across the economy. The data covers the week that included the Memorial Day holiday, which can affect reporting patterns.

The rise in claims comes as the Federal Reserve continues to monitor economic indicators for signs of weakness or strength in the labor market. Worker productivity data was also revised downward in separate government figures, adding to concerns about economic momentum. The labor market has remained a key focus for policymakers as they balance inflation concerns against economic growth.

The spike in gold prices accompanied the jobless claims report, with spot gold reclaiming the $4,500 per ounce level. Precious metals often attract investor interest during periods of economic uncertainty as traders seek safe-haven assets. The movement suggests market participants are reacting to signs of labor market softening.

The current claims level represents the highest since February when geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East. This baseline for comparison underscores how recent labor market conditions have evolved over the past four months. The data will likely influence upcoming Federal Reserve decisions on monetary policy as officials assess whether the labor market is cooling enough to ease inflationary pressures without tipping into recession.

Economic analysts will be watching closely to determine whether this increase represents a temporary spike tied to seasonal reporting variations or a genuine shift in employer hiring decisions. The Memorial Day holiday timing adds some complexity to interpreting the numbers, as holiday weeks can create distortions in weekly filings.

The jobless claims data provides important context for understanding broader labor market health. While 225,000 claims remain relatively moderate by historical standards, the upward movement from recent weeks has caught the attention of investors and policymakers alike. The combination of rising jobless claims and downward productivity revisions suggests the economy may be facing some headwinds that warrant closer monitoring.

The Labor Department will continue releasing weekly claims data, which economists view as among the most timely indicators of labor market conditions. These figures often move before broader employment statistics become available, making them valuable for spotting emerging trends. As the Federal Reserve weighs its next steps on interest rates, this pattern of rising claims will likely feature prominently in policy discussions.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects US-Brokered Cease-Fire With Israel, Fighting Continues
cards.teaser: A renewed cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon collapsed before it could take effect after Hezbollah rejected the US-brokered deal.
cards.body:
A US-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon collapsed after Hezbollah rejected the deal. The Iran-backed group's leader, Naim Qassem, dismissed the plan as a "roadmap to annihilate part of the Lebanese people." Hezbollah was not included in the negotiations between Israel and the Lebanese government, which the United States announced Wednesday night.

The ceasefire required Hezbollah to halt its attacks before Israel would stop its offensive. Israel announced it would continue military operations following the rejection. Israel and Hezbollah subsequently exchanged strikes, casting doubt on the truce and highlighting the difficulty of achieving peace when key militant groups are excluded from diplomatic talks.

cards.headline: Trump plans to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced his intention to nominate acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to lead the Justice Department permanently.
cards.body:
President Trump plans to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general. If confirmed by the Senate, Blanche would become the administration's top prosecutor. He currently serves as acting attorney general at the Department of Justice and previously worked as one of Trump's personal lawyers.

The nomination will require Senate confirmation hearings before Blanche can assume the permanent role.

cards.headline: Trump to announce $700 million in federal support for coal industry
cards.teaser: The president is expected to approve hundreds of millions in taxpayer funding for coal plants and export infrastructure.
cards.body:
President Trump is invoking the Defense Production Act, a Cold War-era statute designed to accelerate industrial output during national emergencies, to distribute $700 million to coal-fired power plants across the US. The grants will support more than a dozen existing coal facilities, including those with export capabilities.

The move represents Trump's continued support for the coal industry, which he has promoted despite coal being the dirtiest fossil fuel. Critics have accused the administration of prioritizing polluters as the coal sector faces economic headwinds from cheaper natural gas and expanding renewable energy sources.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Backs SEC Authority to Seize Illegal Gains
cards.teaser: The justices ruled unanimously that the financial regulator can collect wrongfully obtained money without proving victim losses.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court unanimously ruled in favor of the Securities and Exchange Commission's enforcement powers. The decision allows the SEC to strip wrongdoers of profits from illegal securities activities without proving that specific victims suffered financial losses.

The ruling clarifies the scope of the SEC's disgorgement authority, giving the independent financial watchdog stronger legal standing to pursue enforcement actions against individuals and companies accused of securities violations.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Supports Trump Administration on Telecom Regulation
cards.teaser: The court ruled in favor of federal authority over telecommunications companies in a case involving regulatory oversight.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled in favor of the Trump administration's position on federal telecommunications regulation. The decision clarifies the scope of authority federal agencies hold over telecom companies and their operations.

The case addressed how much regulatory power the government can exercise over communications providers. The court's ruling resolves the dispute over the extent of federal oversight in the telecommunications industry.

cards.headline: 57 percent of Americans say democracy not working in new poll
cards.body:
A majority of Americans believe the democratic system in the United States is not functioning properly, according to a new Quinnipiac University poll. The survey found that 57 percent of respondents said the system of democracy is not working, while 37 percent said they believe it is working. Seven percent did not express an opinion.

The poll reflects broader public sentiment about the health of American democratic institutions during a period marked by political tension across multiple branches of government. The survey measures confidence in the overall functioning of democracy rather than approval of any specific politician or party.

Quinnipiac University regularly conducts national polls examining political and social issues. The organization surveys registered voters across the country through telephone interviews to gauge public opinion on key topics affecting the nation.

The finding that a majority of Americans view democracy as not working represents a significant indicator of public dissatisfaction with how government institutions are operating. Research over recent years has shown that confidence in various democratic institutions, including Congress, the presidency, and the courts, fluctuates considerably based on the political climate and current events.

Public trust in government has varied widely depending on what issues dominate the national conversation at any given time. While specific confidence levels rise and fall, concerns about whether democratic institutions are functioning effectively have appeared across different segments of the population at various points.

The available information from this poll does not include breakdowns of responses by political party affiliation or demographic categories. However, previous polling on similar questions about the state of democracy has typically shown differences in how Republicans, Democrats, and independents assess the current state of democratic function. Despite these differences in perspective, worries about democratic functioning have crossed party lines at different moments in recent history.

The results come as Americans grapple with multiple ongoing controversies involving the executive branch, Congress, and the judiciary. These institutional tensions have contributed to broader questions about whether the democratic system is operating as intended.

The survey adds to a growing body of polling data examining public confidence in government and democratic institutions. As Americans continue to express concerns about how well democracy is working, these measures provide insight into the public's assessment of the nation's political system and its ability to address the challenges facing the country.

hero.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill 11 in Gaza City, Including Women and Children
hero.teaser: Medical officials report that four residential buildings were hit in attacks that killed civilians and Hamas security officials.
hero.body:
Israeli airstrikes on four residential buildings in Gaza City killed 11 people, according to medical officials. Women and children were among those killed in the attacks.

Israel's military said the strikes killed four Hamas security officials. The airstrikes hit residential areas, resulting in civilian casualties alongside the targeted security personnel.

cards.teaser: A renewed cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon collapsed before it could take effect after Hezbollah rejected the US-brokered deal.

cards.headline: Ultra-Orthodox Riots in Israel Intensify Ahead of National Elections
cards.teaser: Haredi protests against military conscription have escalated in recent weeks, revealing deep divisions in Israeli society.
cards.body:
Israel's ultra-Orthodox community, known as Haredim, has intensified protests against mandatory military service, with recent demonstrations turning violent. The riots have shocked many Israelis and underscore growing societal divisions as the country approaches national elections.

The Haredim have traditionally been exempt from military service to pursue religious studies. Recent government efforts to expand conscription have met with fierce resistance from the community, leading to increasingly aggressive protests in recent weeks.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Hampered by Community Mistrust
cards.teaser: Health workers struggle to treat patients and manage burials as residents in a remote mining town question whether the disease is real.
cards.body:
In a remote mining town at the center of the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, grief and mistrust are complicating containment efforts. Health workers are struggling to treat the ill and safely bury the dead according to protocols designed to prevent transmission.

Adding to the challenge, there is no effective vaccine available for the Ebola strain currently spreading in Congo. Several vaccine candidates are undergoing trials, but it remains uncertain how long development will take. The combination of community skepticism and lack of preventive tools has created significant obstacles to stopping the virus.

cards.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
cards.teaser: The Iranian-French author and filmmaker created the acclaimed graphic novel series about growing up during the Islamic Revolution.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian author and illustrator, has died at age 56. She was best known for creating Persepolis, the acclaimed graphic novel memoir that reshaped global perceptions of Iran. The autobiographical work, published in the early 2000s, depicted an Iranian girl's life during the Islamic Revolution and Iran-Iraq War. Her distinctive black-and-white illustrations and intimate storytelling brought the Iranian experience to international audiences, and the work was adapted into an Oscar-nominated film.

According to her family, Satrapi died of sadness following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, last year.

cards.headline: New Zealand Lawmakers Banned From China After Taiwan Visit
cards.teaser: China imposed a one-year travel ban on four members of parliament following their trip to Taiwan.
cards.body:
China has imposed a one-year travel ban on four New Zealand lawmakers following their visit to Taiwan last month. The lawmakers were informed of the restriction upon their return home.

New Zealand's foreign minister expressed surprise at the ban, noting that parliamentarians have visited Taiwan regularly in the past without triggering such consequences. The move marks an escalation in China's response to foreign officials traveling to Taiwan, which Beijing considers part of its territory.

cards.headline: John Bolton Expected to Plead Guilty in Classified Documents Case
cards.teaser: The former national security advisor and Trump critic has reached a deal with prosecutors, sources confirm.
cards.body:
John Bolton, former national security adviser under President Trump, has reached a plea agreement in a classified documents case. According to sources familiar with the matter, Bolton will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information, pending court approval.

Bolton left Trump's first administration and subsequently became a prominent critic of the president. The plea deal represents a significant legal development for the former advisor.

hero.headline: Teen killed, three injured in shooting at Northern California high school graduation
hero.body:
An 18-year-old was killed and three others wounded in a shooting that occurred following a high school graduation ceremony in Fairfield, California. The incident took place after the graduation ceremony for Sem Yeto High School. Among those injured was an 11-year-old child.

Law enforcement responded to the scene after receiving reports of gunfire near the graduation venue. The teenager died either at the scene or shortly after arriving at a hospital. The three injured victims received medical care, though authorities have not disclosed their current conditions.

The shooting prompted Fairfield High School to relocate its own upcoming graduation ceremonies. School officials moved the event to a different location due to safety concerns following the violence that unfolded at the nearby Sem Yeto High graduation.

Gun violence at school events has become an ongoing concern across the United States. Graduation ceremonies, which typically draw large crowds including students, families, and community members, have increasingly become sites of such incidents in recent years. Law enforcement agencies have responded by implementing stronger security measures at these gatherings.

Police have not yet released details about a suspect or the motive behind the shooting. Investigators are still working to determine what sparked the gunfire and whether the shooter had any relationship to the school or any of those attending the ceremony. The community in Fairfield, situated in Northern California between Sacramento and San Francisco, is dealing with the aftermath of violence that transformed what should have been a celebration into a tragedy.

The incident adds to a troubling pattern of mass shootings in California and across the nation. School administrators and law enforcement officials are increasingly grappling with how to balance open celebration and commemoration of student achievements with the need to protect attendees from potential violence.

Fairfield community members and school officials have expressed concern about the safety of future school events. The decision to relocate Fairfield High School's graduation reflects the heightened anxiety many institutions now feel when planning large public gatherings on school property.

Authorities have set up tip lines and continue investigating the incident. They are asking anyone with information about the shooting to come forward to help identify the shooter and understand what led to the violence. The investigation remains ongoing as law enforcement works to piece together the circumstances that led to the shooting and the identity of the person responsible.

cards.headline: Trump plans to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced his intention to nominate acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to lead the Justice Department permanently.
cards.body:
President Trump plans to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general. If confirmed by the Senate, Blanche would become the administration's top prosecutor. He currently serves as acting attorney general at the Department of Justice and previously worked as one of Trump's personal lawyers.

The nomination will require Senate confirmation hearings before Blanche can assume the permanent role.

cards.headline: John Bolton to plead guilty in classified documents case
cards.teaser: Former National Security Advisor John Bolton reached a plea deal with prosecutors over his handling of classified information.
cards.body:
John Bolton, former National Security Advisor under President Trump, has reached a plea agreement in a classified documents case. The deal allows him to plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information, pending court approval.

Bolton departed the Trump administration in September 2019 after policy disagreements and later became a vocal critic of the president. The Justice Department filed charges against him in 2025 as part of ongoing cases involving mishandling of classified materials.

The move represents Trump's continued support for the coal industry, which he has promoted despite coal being the dirtiest fossil fuel. Critics have accused the administration of prioritizing polluters as the coal sector faces economic headwinds from cheaper natural gas and expanding renewable energy sources.

cards.headline: New York transit system prepares for World Cup and NBA Finals crowds
cards.teaser: Transit officials are planning to accommodate up to 100,000 additional daily travelers arriving for major sporting events.
cards.body:
New York City transit officials are preparing the mass transit system to accommodate up to 100,000 additional travelers per day as fans arrive for FIFA World Cup matches across the New York and New Jersey metropolitan area.

Transit authorities are coordinating service expansions and crowd management strategies to prevent system overload during the events.

cards.headline: Liverpool appoints Andoni Iraola as head coach
cards.teaser: The Premier League club hired Iraola on a two-year contract following the dismissal of Arne Slot.
cards.body:
Liverpool have appointed Andoni Iraola as their new head coach on a two-year contract, replacing Arne Slot who was sacked just six days earlier. The 43-year-old Spanish coach previously managed Bournemouth, where he worked with Liverpool's sporting director Richard Hughes.

Iraola emerged as Liverpool's preferred candidate after the club identified him as ideal for their desired playing style. Several other clubs, including Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace, had also pursued the Basque manager, though Liverpool moved swiftly to secure their top target.

cards.headline: Royal Navy identifies three crew members killed in helicopter crash
cards.teaser: The Ministry of Defence named the service members who died in a recent naval aviation accident.
cards.body:
The Royal Navy has identified three crew members who died in a helicopter crash: Lieutenant Commander Chris Gayson, 42, Lieutenant Lily-Mae Fisher, 31, and Petty Officer Owen Green, 24. The Ministry of Defence released their names after notifying their families.

Tributes have been paid to the three service members, who were all active-duty Royal Navy personnel working in naval aviation roles.

cards.headline: Dow Gains Over 500 Points While Nasdaq Falls After Broadcom Earnings
cards.teaser: Stock markets moved in opposite directions as chip stocks declined following Broadcom's quarterly results.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 500 points while the Nasdaq Composite declined, reflecting divergent performance across market sectors. Broadcom's disappointing earnings report triggered a selloff in semiconductor stocks, weighing heavily on the technology-focused Nasdaq.

Broadcom shares fell along with other chip manufacturers. The weakness in semiconductors pressured the Nasdaq, while strength in other sectors supported gains in the Dow Jones.

cards.headline: Fire Causes Major Damage at Tata Steel Plant in Wales
cards.teaser: A blaze at the Port Talbot facility damaged a production line and prompted officials to warn residents to keep windows closed.
cards.body:
A fire at the Tata Steel facility in Port Talbot, Wales has caused substantial damage to a production line. Firefighters worked to control the blaze as the company assessed the full extent of the operational impact.

Local authorities advised residents near the plant to keep their windows and doors closed while crews battled the flames.

cards.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Public Stock Offering
cards.teaser: Individual investors will be able to purchase shares in Elon Musk's aerospace and AI company starting next week.
cards.body:
SpaceX is planning a historic initial public offering targeting $75 billion in fundraising, which would give the company a market valuation of $1.77 trillion. The stock market debut is scheduled for June 12 and aims to be the largest IPO ever.

Founder Elon Musk stands to become extraordinarily wealthy from the offering. As the world's wealthiest person, a successful launch at these valuations could position him to become the first trillionaire.

cards.headline: CBS Fires Scott Pelley From 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The veteran journalist's dismissal is the latest in a series of staff changes at the network's news division.
cards.body:
CBS fired Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes on Tuesday following clashes with the network's new management. Pelley responded with a public statement accusing CBS executives of instructing him to inject "falsehoods and bias" into his reporting and of silencing employees.

Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes has been America's top program for decades because audiences trust its integrity and quality. His firing is part of broader turmoil affecting CBS News's operations.

hero.headline: NASA ends MAVEN mission after 11 years studying Mars atmosphere
hero.body:
NASA officially concluded the MAVEN mission after the spacecraft spent more than a decade orbiting Mars. The Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution orbiter, which launched in 2013 and arrived at Mars in 2014, stopped communicating with Earth earlier this year. NASA held a media call to formally announce the end of the mission.

Over 11 years, MAVEN studied the Martian atmosphere and investigated how the planet lost much of its air and water over billions of years. The spacecraft was equipped with instruments designed to measure atmospheric composition, track interactions between solar wind and the planet's upper atmosphere, and observe how gases escaped into space. This research helped scientists understand the dramatic transformation of Mars from a potentially habitable world with liquid water on its surface to the cold, dry planet visible today.

The mission team experienced the conclusion with deep emotion. One team member described the loss in personal terms, saying the group felt as though they had lost a loved one when the mission ended. MAVEN significantly exceeded its original planned lifespan, continuing to transmit valuable data for years after its primary mission phase concluded.

The spacecraft fell silent months before NASA announced the official end. Ground controllers lost contact with MAVEN and were unable to restore communication despite repeated attempts. Scientists believe the spacecraft either exhausted its fuel or experienced a critical system failure that prevented it from properly orienting its antenna toward Earth.

MAVEN's contributions fundamentally transformed how scientists understand planetary atmospheres and climate processes on other worlds. The mission provided essential data about how solar radiation and solar wind gradually strip away atmospheric particles, a mechanism that thinned Mars's atmosphere over geological timescales. This understanding has broader implications for studying atmospheric loss on other planets and evaluating the long-term habitability of worlds throughout our solar system and beyond.

The loss of MAVEN reflects the reality of space exploration, where spacecraft eventually reach the end of their operational lives despite the dedication of mission teams. However, the data MAVEN collected during its 11 years in orbit will continue to inform Mars research for decades to come. Scientists will analyze the observations to refine models of planetary atmospheres and improve understanding of how worlds lose their protective air.

MAVEN's legacy demonstrates how sustained observation from orbit can reveal fundamental processes shaping planetary evolution. The spacecraft's instruments captured detailed measurements that ground-based observations and brief orbital passes could never provide. As NASA continues exploring Mars with other missions, MAVEN's findings will serve as a foundation for future discoveries about the red planet's past and its potential for past habitability.

cards.headline: Sun produces three large solar flares, raising northern lights forecasts
cards.teaser: Three major solar flares erupted from the sun in less than 24 hours, increasing the chances of auroras visible across much of the United States.
cards.body:
The sun released three large solar flares within a 24-hour period, creating conditions for enhanced auroral displays. The activity originated from a sunspot and sent coronal mass ejections toward Earth. Forecasters predicted auroras could be visible in 23 states.

The solar eruptions raised geomagnetic activity levels and increased the likelihood of northern lights appearing at lower latitudes than typical. The flares and associated plasma clouds travel through space before interacting with Earth's magnetic field, creating the colorful atmospheric displays.

cards.headline: Bumblebees demonstrate tool use and problem solving in research study
cards.teaser: Bumblebees showed the ability to use tools and solve problems without training, displaying cognitive abilities researchers compared to those seen in primates.
cards.body:
Researchers found that bumblebees can spontaneously solve complex problems using tools, according to a new study. The insects demonstrated these abilities despite having brains far smaller than those of mammals like chimpanzees. The findings challenge assumptions about the relationship between brain size and cognitive capability.

The bumblebees used objects as tools to accomplish tasks they had not been trained to perform. One researcher said the bees surprise them every time with their problem-solving abilities. The study adds to growing evidence that insect cognition is more sophisticated than previously understood.

cards.headline: Helion raises $465 million for Microsoft fusion power plant
cards.teaser: The Sam Altman-backed fusion energy startup secured new funding to build a power plant for Microsoft with a target completion date of 2028.
cards.body:
Helion, the fusion startup backed by Sam Altman, has raised $465 million in fresh funding to support its power plant project for Microsoft. The company is racing to complete the facility by 2028 under its agreement with the tech giant.

Fusion energy works by fusing atomic nuclei to release power, mimicking the process that fuels the sun. The technology is pursued as a potential source of clean, abundant electricity, though no commercial fusion plant has yet achieved net energy production at scale.

cards.headline: Apple approves first AI agent for Messages for Business platform
cards.teaser: Poke became the first AI agent approved to operate on Apple's Messages for Business, letting people interact with AI through text messages.
cards.body:
Poke has become the first AI agent approved for Apple's Messages for Business platform. The startup enables users to interact with AI tools directly through text messages, eliminating the need to download separate applications or navigate unfamiliar interfaces.

This approval represents a significant step in Apple's efforts to integrate AI capabilities into its messaging ecosystem. By leveraging the accessibility of text-based communication, Poke makes AI functionality available to anyone with a phone capable of using Apple's business messaging system.

cards.headline: Meta builds data centers using tents to cut costs
cards.teaser: Meta adopted a construction approach previously used by Tesla, housing data center equipment in large tent structures rather than traditional buildings.
cards.body:
Meta found a way to reduce its data center expenses by using tent structures instead of conventional buildings. The company took the approach from Tesla, which has used temporary structures for manufacturing operations. The tents house the servers and equipment needed for Meta's computing infrastructure.

Data centers represent a major capital expense for technology companies, requiring massive facilities to cool and power thousands of servers. The tent approach may allow Meta to deploy computing capacity more quickly and at lower cost than building permanent structures.

cards.headline: Apple expected to unveil revamped Siri at WWDC 2026
cards.teaser: Apple's developer conference is set to feature a major update to Siri, with new AI capabilities developed with help from Google and Nvidia.
cards.body:
Apple plans to introduce a significantly updated version of Siri at its Worldwide Developers Conference. The voice assistant will launch in September with new AI features. Apple worked with Google and Nvidia to develop the enhanced capabilities as part of its Apple Intelligence initiative.

The conference will also showcase iOS 27 and other software updates. WWDC represents a key moment for Apple to demonstrate its AI strategy as competitors have released their own generative AI products. Tim Cook is expected to use the event to outline the company's vision for artificial intelligence across its product line.

hero.headline: Liverpool appoint Andoni Iraola as head coach after Arne Slot dismissal
hero.body:
Liverpool have appointed Andoni Iraola as their new head coach on a two-year contract, just six days after dismissing Arne Slot. The 43-year-old Spanish manager, who previously led Bournemouth, was identified as the ideal fit for Liverpool's preferred playing style.

The club moved swiftly to secure Iraola despite competition from other top European sides. Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace all expressed interest in the Basque coach, but Liverpool were his only option in formal talks. The club also considered Stuttgart's Sebastian Hoeness and Pierre Sage of Lens before settling on Iraola as their preferred choice.

Richard Hughes, Liverpool's sporting director who previously worked with Iraola at Bournemouth, led the appointment process. Hughes and Michael Edwards, chief executive of football for owners Fenway Sports Group, conducted a review into the team's poor title defence under Slot and concluded that a managerial change was necessary to implement a more aggressive, attacking approach.

Iraola made clear from the start that Liverpool were his only desired destination following the expiry of his Bournemouth contract. Negotiations progressed smoothly once formal talks began earlier this week. The manager arrived on Merseyside on Thursday and has signed a contract through the end of the 2027/28 season.

Speaking to Liverpool's media channel, Iraola expressed his ambitions for the role. "I understand where I'm coming and what is expected. I'm ready for the challenge," he said. He also outlined his desire to prove himself quickly and become fully integrated with the club. "Football is about emotions, about passion," Iraola added. "No better place than Anfield."

When asked about his ambitions, Iraola acknowledged the challenge ahead. "Liverpool gives me the chance to coach top players, and top players give you the chance to fight for titles. To win titles. Obviously when you arrive at a place, you cannot promise everything. But I'm ready for the challenge."

Iraola intends to bring his backroom team from Bournemouth to Liverpool, including assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper, analyst Tom Webber and fitness coach Pablo de la Torre. However, Liverpool have not yet finalized all additions to their new coaching staff, with Elphick and Cooper still under contract with Bournemouth.

Liverpool view Iraola as one of the best available coaches and believe he is well-suited to evolving the team's playing style. The club was particularly attracted by his proven success in the Premier League, where he gradually improved Bournemouth year-on-year despite limited resources. His ability to develop individual players and implement high-pressing football also influenced the decision.

The two-year deal reflects Iraola's preferred approach to managing his career at previous clubs, though it is relatively short by Liverpool's historical standards.

cards.headline: Fan receives lifetime NBA ban after running onto court for Victor Wembanyama selfie
cards.teaser: The NBA issued a lifetime ban to a fan who ran onto the court during Game 1 of the Finals attempting to take a selfie with Victor Wembanyama.
cards.body:
A fan was banned from all NBA arenas for life after running onto the court during Game 1 of the NBA Finals to take a selfie with Victor Wembanyama. The incident triggered an immediate security response, and the NBA confirmed that two fans received lifetime bans in connection with the selfie attempt.

In a separate matter, the league is investigating an incident involving New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson, who became upset during an interaction with fans in the fourth quarter of his team's 105-95 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.

cards.headline: Ollie Robinson takes four wickets as England lead New Zealand by 79 runs
cards.teaser: Ollie Robinson marked his return to Test cricket with four wickets at Lord's as New Zealand closed the first day on 61-6, trailing England by 79 runs.
cards.body:
Ollie Robinson marked his return to Test cricket after more than two years with a stunning performance, taking four wickets as England gained the upper hand against New Zealand on day one at Lord's. Robinson claimed three of his wickets in his first over back, a devastating spell that energized England after they had been bowled out for 140.

The opening day proved dramatic, with 16 wickets falling across just 60 overs of rain-affected play. New Zealand closed on 61-6, giving England a 79-run lead heading into day two. Robinson's remarkable comeback gave the hosts control despite their modest first-innings total.

cards.headline: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska reaches French Open final
cards.teaser: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska advanced to the French Open final where she will face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva.
cards.body:
Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska advanced to the French Open final with a 7-6, 6-4 victory over Diana Shnaider. The remarkable run through qualifying rounds has put her one win away from claiming the title.

Chwalinska will face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in the championship match. Andreeva reached the final by defeating Marta Kostyuk in her semifinal. A Grand Slam title would represent a fairytale triumph for Chwalinska.

cards.headline: Manchester United will not overpay in summer transfer window, says chief executive
cards.teaser: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada said the club will not bow to pressure and overpay during the upcoming summer transfer window.
cards.body:
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has reaffirmed the club will not overpay for players in the summer transfer window, refusing to be swayed by external pressure. The stance reflects United's commitment to financial discipline in their recruitment strategy.

Berrada has also addressed the future of captain Bruno Fernandes, stating the club wants the 31-year-old to remain at Old Trafford. However, he has not ruled out the possibility of Fernandes leaving, acknowledging mixed messages from the midfielder about his future at the club.

cards.headline: England star Ellie Kildunne seeking new club after Harlequins exit
cards.teaser: England rugby player Ellie Kildunne said she did not want to leave Harlequins and does not know where she will play next season.
cards.body:
England international Ellie Kildunne has confirmed her departure from Harlequins and is now searching for a new club. The rugby star says she did not want to leave the club and has no confirmed destination for next season.

Kildunne is open to offers from interested parties and has invited clubs to contact her as she evaluates her options for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Senate college sports proposal
cards.teaser: Former President Donald Trump endorsed a Senate proposal aimed at reforming college sports, calling it the last chance to save the system.
cards.body:
Former President Donald Trump voiced support for the Protect College Sports Act, a Senate bill aimed at addressing college athletics reform. Trump described the legislation as the last chance to save college sports as the Senate considers the proposal.

Former Alabama coach Nick Saban testified before Congress asking lawmakers to bring order to college sports through the bill. The legislation faces opposition from the SEC and Big Ten conferences.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist and graphic novelist whose memoir Persepolis transformed international understanding of Iran, has died at 56. Her family said she "died of sadness" following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, who passed away on April 8 of the previous year.

Satrapi was born in 1969 in Rasht, Iran, and grew up in Tehran with her father, an engineer, and her mother, a dress designer. As a teenager, her parents sent her to Europe to continue her education and protect her from restrictions under the Islamic Republic. She eventually settled in France, arriving in 1994 and becoming a French citizen in 2006.

In 2000, while still an arts student in Strasbourg with limited professional comics experience, Satrapi published Persepolis. She initially had modest hopes for the work, telling El País in 2020: "With Persepolis, I didn't even think I'd find a publisher. I thought I'd make 50 photocopies for my friends to read." Instead, the graphic memoir became an international publishing phenomenon, selling millions of copies and establishing her as one of the most widely read Iranian authors worldwide.

The autobiographical work depicted her childhood during Iran's Islamic Revolution, following a rebellious young girl as she navigated the country's violence and ideological control before being sent alone to Europe at age 14. Satrapi explained to the Guardian in 2024 that she aimed to help Western readers recognize "Oh, they're actually human beings like us" when thinking about Iranian people.

President Emmanuel Macron paid tribute, saying Satrapi was "a great artist who turned her Iranian childhood into a universal tale," noting her "childlike perspective, her irony, her tenderness, her inner demons."

Satrapi co-directed the 2007 animated film adaptation of Persepolis, becoming the first woman nominated for an Academy Award for best animated feature. She later directed five feature films, including Radioactive in 2019, starring Rosamund Pike as scientist Marie Curie.

Regarding her chosen medium, Satrapi said in 2012: "Drawing – it's the first language of human beings, before writing, before even talking, before words." She explained that her comics aimed to reassure young Iranians they were heard and supported globally, stating: "If they kill you and the whole world doesn't care, how is that? This is the whole thing I'm asking: just recognise this."

After stepping away from comics for years, Satrapi returned to the medium in 2024 with Woman, Life, Freedom, a collaborative graphic work examining the protest movement following the death of Kurdish-Iranian woman Mahsa Amini in 2022. She told the Guardian: "The only thing I can do is cultural work. This book is a message to the Iranian people to say, listen, you are not alone."

cards.headline: CBS Fires Three 60 Minutes Correspondents Including Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: CBS News has terminated three correspondents from its flagship news program 60 Minutes, including longtime correspondent Scott Pelley.
cards.body:
CBS News fired three correspondents from 60 Minutes, including longtime journalist Scott Pelley. In a public statement, Pelley accused the network's new executives of silencing employees and instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He claimed executives pushed unverified claims and gave politicians input in interviews.

Pelley defended the program's decades-long success, attributing it to integrity and quality storytelling. Commentary compared his firing to pivotal moments in journalism history when reporters challenged powerful institutions, suggesting Pelley was fired for upholding journalistic principles that CBS's new management rejected.

cards.headline: Advance Ticket Sales for The Odyssey Overwhelm AMC Website
cards.teaser: Christopher Nolan's upcoming film The Odyssey has generated such demand that wait times on AMC's website dropped from one hour to eight minutes.
cards.body:
Advance ticket sales for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey initially created hour-long wait times on AMC Theatres' website before improving to eight minutes. Multiple outlets reported on the difficulties customers faced when attempting to purchase tickets for the anticipated film.

The Seattle International Film Festival announced it will bring back 70mm screenings for the movie, while Westwood's Village Theatre scheduled a three-week 70mm run. The high demand reflects continued interest in Nolan's work and large-format theatrical presentations.

cards.headline: Bill Ackman to Sell $290.5 Million in Universal Music Stock After Takeover Bid Rejected
cards.teaser: Universal Music will repurchase over 14.2 million shares from Pershing Square after rejecting a takeover proposal from the investment firm.
cards.body:
Universal Music announced it will repurchase approximately $290.5 million worth of stock from Pershing Square, the investment fund founded by billionaire Bill Ackman. The buyback involves over 14.2 million shares valued at about 250 million euros.

The transaction follows Universal Music's rejection of a takeover proposal from Pershing Square. As the world's largest record company, Universal Music's decision to repurchase the shares marks a significant change in its relationship with one of its major investors.

cards.headline: Sadie Sink to Star in FX Limited Series Based on The Marriage Plot
cards.teaser: FX has greenlit The Marriage Plot, a limited series adaptation of Jeffrey Eugenides' 2011 novel starring Sadie Sink.
cards.body:
FX ordered The Marriage Plot, a limited series based on Jeffrey Eugenides' 2011 novel, with Sadie Sink in the lead role. Will Arbery will write the adaptation and Hiro Murai will direct. The series will stream on Hulu and is produced by A24.

The story follows three recent college graduates navigating relationships and life decisions after graduation. The project represents a collaboration between FX, A24, and the creative team behind the adaptation of Eugenides' literary work.

cards.headline: The Beatles Release Colorized All You Need Is Love Performance Video
cards.teaser: The Beatles will mark Global Beatles Day with a colorized video of their All You Need Is Love performance being published officially online for the first time.
cards.body:
The Beatles are releasing a colorized version of their All You Need Is Love performance to commemorate Global Beatles Day. The video marks the first time the performance has been officially published online.

The release continues efforts to make historic Beatles performances more accessible to modern audiences through restoration and digital distribution. The colorization aims to bring new visual dimension to the classic recording.

cards.headline: New York Officials Release PSA Promoting City as Film Production Hub
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office released a public service announcement featuring Spike Lee, Amy Schumer, and other filmmakers promoting New York as a filming destination.
cards.body:
New York City's office of media and entertainment unveiled a promotional campaign featuring acclaimed filmmakers Spike Lee, Amy Schumer, John Krasinski, Natasha Lyonne, Darren Aronofsky, and Celine Song. The PSA highlights New York as an attractive destination for film production.

The campaign emphasizes the city's streamlined processes for filmmakers, positioning New York as the easiest place in the country to produce films. The initiative aims to draw more production work to the city by showcasing both its simplified regulations and local creative talent.

hero.headline: 57 percent of Americans say democracy not working in new poll
hero.body:
A majority of Americans believe the democratic system in the United States is not functioning properly, according to a new Quinnipiac University poll. The survey found that 57 percent of respondents said the system of democracy is not working, while 37 percent said they believe it is working. Seven percent did not express an opinion.

The poll reflects broader public sentiment about the health of American democratic institutions during a period marked by political tension across multiple branches of government. The survey measures confidence in the overall functioning of democracy rather than approval of any specific politician or party.

Quinnipiac University regularly conducts national polls examining political and social issues. The organization surveys registered voters across the country through telephone interviews to gauge public opinion on key topics affecting the nation.

The finding that a majority of Americans view democracy as not working represents a significant indicator of public dissatisfaction with how government institutions are operating. Research over recent years has shown that confidence in various democratic institutions, including Congress, the presidency, and the courts, fluctuates considerably based on the political climate and current events.

Public trust in government has varied widely depending on what issues dominate the national conversation at any given time. While specific confidence levels rise and fall, concerns about whether democratic institutions are functioning effectively have appeared across different segments of the population at various points.

The available information from this poll does not include breakdowns of responses by political party affiliation or demographic categories. However, previous polling on similar questions about the state of democracy has typically shown differences in how Republicans, Democrats, and independents assess the current state of democratic function. Despite these differences in perspective, worries about democratic functioning have crossed party lines at different moments in recent history.

The results come as Americans grapple with multiple ongoing controversies involving the executive branch, Congress, and the judiciary. These institutional tensions have contributed to broader questions about whether the democratic system is operating as intended.

The survey adds to a growing body of polling data examining public confidence in government and democratic institutions. As Americans continue to express concerns about how well democracy is working, these measures provide insight into the public's assessment of the nation's political system and its ability to address the challenges facing the country.

cards.headline: Appeals court blocks order for Customs chief to testify on tariff refunds
cards.teaser: A federal appeals court agreed to halt an order requiring the head of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to testify about tariff refunds.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court on Thursday agreed to halt an order requiring the head of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to testify next week about tariff refunds. The Trump administration is fighting the order, arguing a judge overstepped by compelling CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott to appear in a New York City courtroom.

The appeals court granted the stay, blocking Scott from having to testify as scheduled. The case involves questions about the administration of tariff refunds by CBP. The Trump administration has challenged the authority of the lower court judge to compel testimony from the agency head.

cards.headline: Fetterman announces opposition to Blanche for attorney general
cards.teaser: Sen. John Fetterman said he will vote against the confirmation of acting Attorney General Todd Blanche.
cards.body:
Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania announced Thursday that he will vote against confirming Todd Blanche as attorney general. Blanche currently serves as acting attorney general while awaiting potential formal nomination and Senate confirmation.

The Pennsylvania Democrat joins other lawmakers who have expressed opposition to the nomination. Trump's former personal lawyer would become the administration's top prosecutor if confirmed by the Senate.

cards.headline: Six Republican senators join Democrats to vote for White House ballroom restrictions
cards.teaser: Six GOP senators voted with Democrats on a proposal to block construction of President Trump's White House ballroom without congressional authorization.
cards.body:
Six Republican senators voted with Democrats in support of a proposal to block the construction of President Trump's 90,000-square-foot White House ballroom unless Congress authorizes the project. Sen. Jeff Merkley of Oregon sponsored the amendment.

The amendment would have given Congress sole authority to construct a new ballroom and would have barred any federal funds or private financing for the project without explicit congressional approval. The proposal sought to require legislative authorization before moving forward with the large-scale construction project at the White House complex.

cards.headline: Democratic senators question tobacco companies on FDA lobbying
cards.teaser: Six Democratic senators sent letters to two tobacco companies asking for details on their dealings with the Trump administration after the FDA eased vaping restrictions.
cards.body:
A group of six Democratic senators sent letters to two tobacco companies on Thursday, asking for details on their dealings with the Trump administration. The inquiry comes after the Food and Drug Administration eased restrictions on vaping products.

Last month, the FDA granted marketing authorization to four flavored vaping products and issued new guidance allowing additional products on the market. The senators are seeking information about the companies' communications with the administration in the period leading up to the policy change.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary results
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in early results from California's gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
California's gubernatorial primary results remain unsettled as state election officials continue counting uncounted ballots, a process that could take days or weeks. Republican Steve Hilton is narrowly leading the race, followed by Democrat Xavier Becerra, with billionaire Tom Steyer trailing behind.

Under California's primary system, the top two vote-getters advance to the general election, regardless of party affiliation. The winners will face off to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former official in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. She will compete in the general election for the state's top executive office.

If elected in November, Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.
